Home Hijacking

By: Graham Coetzer | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Homeowners in suburban Boksburg are waging war against Congolese and Nigerian nationals who have hijacked their units and now run the estate from Hell

Unique Selling Point:
We have been approached by 20 plus homeowners, some of who still owe bonds on their units in Eveleigh Estate, who say their houses have been hijacked by foreign nationals. The foreigners do not pay rent, elec, water or levies to the owners. Instead they are paying rent to Congolese kingpin Peter Ngaula, who is acting as the dayfactor landlord and illegally occupying the units. Attempts to get police involved have failed, and residents say the eviction process is unaffordable in the high court, and takes up to a year

Further information:
In a meeting between Wynand, Anna-Maria and Chwayitisa it has been decided we can join residents on Saturday 7 July as they are going to block off all access to the estate from the outside, with our presenter and camera crew. The residents have had it with the goings on and are hoping to get SAPS to at the very least arrest Kingpin Peter. It has also been decided not to attempt to get a police raid at the site. This means that after saturday it might not be possible for us to get access to the complex to film inside with our presenter. We will try to do this on saturday depending on the situation on the ground and safety. We do NOT as yet have clear footage of Peter. Will attempt to get saturday also. We have Peter's lawyers details. I have given his passport number to Interpol to see if he is, as was alleged to me, a fugitive from justice in the DRC.

We have CCTV footage showing the following:
Alleged drug deals
Alleged bribery of Police by Peter
Alleged vehicle theft
Violent fights between rival Congolese gangs
Congolese blocking access to estate with vehicles
Congolese destroying Biometric access unit, twice!

We have hidden camera visuals of the following:
Alleged drug deals
Eviction of two hijacked units, with residents becoming violent

Press Release:


In an upwardly mobile residential complex on Gauteng’s East Rand, suburban bliss has turned to living hell as cunning building hijackers have systematically muscled in to take over one unit after another. Refusing to pay for rent, levies, water or electricity, they’re openly engaging in drug dealing and turf wars. Owners of the bonded townhouses are left having to pay their mortgages, while their children are at risk from the violence and intimidation. Law enforcement has been little help. Can home owners wrestle back their properties?

Script:


Hijacked Houses
11 July 2018
Voice
Eveleigh Estate, nestled in suburban Boksburg, was developed as an upwardly mobile complex with 243, two and three bedroom units - for many homeowners it should have been an investor’s dream.

Link Mcfarlane
This may look like an ordinary estate, but why are resident’s here calling this the complex from hell?

Sound Up Alice
It’s like the crime hub of Boksburg, Eveleigh Estate is a criminal complex, there’s no doubt about it.

Voice
This woman, who we’ll call Alice, owns an apartment in the complex, where she lives with her husband and young child.

Sound Up Alice
We’ve been living there for three years now, and initially it looked like a beautiful place.

Voice
But owners we’ve spoken to say their suburban bliss has turned into a living nightmare since 47 of the homes in the estate have been hijacked by illegal tenants. The estate has literally become a war zone between homeowners on one side, and the hijackers on the other.

Sound Up Alice
It’s horrifying… Witnessing what we witness on a daily basis.

Voice
It’s a scary thought but this could happen in any complex, anywhere in the country. At Eveleigh the home hijackers simply stopped paying rent or utility bills, and refused to move out. Some of the empty units were even taken by force. Owners say the kingpin behind the hijackings is this Congolese man, the illusive Peter Ngaula. He allegedly earns an income from renting out the hijacked homes.

Sound Up Alice
Any criminal activity, Peter is a part of it.

Voice
Alice says many of Peter Ngaula’s tenants are drug dealers who peddle their wares 24/7 at the estate. Our investigators caught this footage on hidden camera.

Sound Up Alice
And you’ll see the customer stop, the drug dealer walks up to the car, makes it look like a casual talk, and you’ll see his hand goes into the car. He takes the cash, turns around and walks back in.

Voice
The estate’s cctv cameras have also picked up the alleged drug deals. But that’s only the beginning. Raphael Makhatshaba is the chairman of the Eveleigh Body Corporate. He says Ngaula’s tenants frequently destroy the estate’s expensive biometric fingerprint scanner as happened here in May this year

Sound Up Raphael
The reason they are breaking the biometric system, it is because, people they rent to cannot get fingerprint registration. So they struggle in and out of the complex. So the best thing for them is to make the gate not work. In that way everyone will walk in and out, which is compromising the whole safety of the complex.

Voice
Alice says their homes have also become the scene of regular violent fights between the hijackers.

Sound Up Alice
Peter, the Congolese, the Nigerians, all of them, as soon as there is a spat, it’s like a massive crowd that gathers. They don’t know why they are fighting, they just fight. And it get’s so bad that they physically come and fight by your unit. And as soon as you ask stop, then you get threatened.

Voice
Things came to a head last week saturday when Makhatshaba called for the removal of Ngaula and his henchman from the complex. We arrived at the tense scene just in time to catch security dressed in full riot gear, and ironically, the EFF who had also come to help the homeowners regain control of their properties.

Sound Up Macfarlane
So we’ve just arrived in Boksburg at Eveleigh Estate, as you can see there in the background there is already action that is taking place. We don’t know what is going on but everybody is now moving inside because the residents here, are fed up with what has been happening here.

Voice
Addressing a group of owners and tenants Makhatshaba said they had tried everything in their power to stop the criminal behaviour at Eveleigh.

Sound Up Raphael Makhatshaba
We have tried to reason with them - stop damaging our property, fight your evictions in court.

Voice
He also said cases they had laid against Ngaula and his group had been ignored by the police.

Sound Up Raphael Makhatshaba
…nothing done, the docket closed on the 30th of January 2018 by CC Mbambo. We have over ten of these cases I don’t want to read all of them.

Voice
Ngaula, who had apparently got word of Makhatshaba’s plans, was nowhere to be seen.

Sound Up Raphael
Today is the last time I will see Peter, or Jannick or Solomon in this property.

Voice
And with that they set off to evict the occupants of two units, one of them where Ngaula allegedly stays. Shimi Mahlaela, who was not involved with Saturday’s events, bought 4 apartments in Eveleigh at an auction, hoping to earn rental income from his investment. Unfortunately the units were already occupied by the hijackers.

Sound Up Shimi Mahlaela
At the moment, I’m owing more than a million in levies and rates and taxes. I’ve lost half a million in legal fees.

Voice
The half a million went to legal fees to obtain eviction orders on his units. These cellphone images show the Sheriff of the court carrying out one of the evictions last week. But as soon as the sheriff left, the tenants apparently fought their way back into the estate.

Sound Up Cellphone footage

Voice
On saturday morning Makhatshaba called for police to come and face the angry residents.

Sound Up Raphael
And I want the Boksburg Police Commander, I want him to come here, or if it’s her she needs to come here. We will not have this continued.

Voice
But the commander must have been otherwise engaged, so he sent a Seargeant Chauke to attend to the matter.

Sound Up Sergeant Chauke
Good morning everyone, I am Sergeant Chauke from Boksburg North SAPS. I’ve been sent by station commander, Col Mbatla, to come and receive the memorandum on his behalf.

Voice
The sergeant warned the crowd that what they were doing was illegal, but tempers flared.

Sound Up EFF Supporter
The problem is the police that have failed us. Everybody at Boksburg North Police station, they know exactly what is happening here. Because they are on the payroll of these kingpins that are selling drugs in here. Hey brother there’s Mogosha’s here man, left right and center. There’s drugs being sold here. The very same police from Boksburg North they are coming here to, I don’t want to mention it, but they are coming here to buy from here. And we’ve got footage of them. We’ve got proof. When you go to Boksburg North Police station the police officers are taking selfies. You are sitting there and waiting. You can’t do that anymore.

Voice
The sergeant did not want to comment on the allegations, saying he was phoning his commander, and then promptly left the premises. Residents believe Peter Ngaula and his cronies are paying bribes to police officials because of footage like this. In it Ngaula is seen handing something to an unknown police officer after yet another violent altercation.

Sound Up Raphael
Macfarlane: When you speak to Peter what does he say, have you tried to engage with these people?

Raphael: I’ve engaged with Peter so many times. He says I must stay away from his unit.

Voice
As the forced evictions continued, we were tipped off that some of the dealers had hidden drugs next to the swimming pool area, so we decided to go and investigate. Searching the plants next to the swimming pool wall we found the typical used drug paraphernalia and, without much effort, also this.

Sound Up Macfarlane
Now if you come in closer here, we came across this bag over here. Look at this, one, two, three, four, five, six, seven grams of - we don’t know if it’s Cocaine, whether it’s KHAT, or Heroin, we don’t know what it is. One can’t even begin to imagine, if your child were to be playing around here and to find this bag… Anything can happen.

Sound Up “Alice”
You don’t want to live there knowing my child’s going to see this, or finding drugs in your garden. Right in front of your unit, knowing my child played there ten minutes before that.

Voice
Meanwhile,the inevitable confrontation between residents and the hijackers was looming as some of the hijackers decided to protect Peter Ngaula’s apartment. Brandishing sticks, bricks and pepper spray, they threatened our crew and the residents.

Sound Up Macfarlane
So the situation is getting quite tense, the people that have occupied this house have now arrived, as you can see they are very enraged and very angry. They are saying the owner of the place is not here so they are not going to let them come in here.

Voice
And within seconds violence broke out as one of the hijackers sprayed the security with pepper spray…

Sound Up Fight footage

Voice
After a chaotic chase to the front gates and back through the complex concluded, security managed to calm the man and protect him from the angry mob.

Sound Up Woman crying

Voice
Back at the apartment the eviction was briefly halted because of a surprise left by the previous occupants.

Sound Up Macfarlane
So we’ve gotten into the house now, they’ve sprayed pepper spray in trying to protect this home that has also been hijacked. The pepper spray is quite strong because they don’t want anybody coming in here. But they have opened to get some ventilation and hopefully try and move their things out. As they said this is a house that has been occupied for quite a while and they also believe that some illegal drug activity has been happening here.

Voice
So here’s the shocker, despite everything that you’ve just seen, the reality is that under the Prevention of Illegal Eviction, or PIE act, the only way to legally evict the hijackers would be to go to court and obtain an eviction order. Attorney Cilna Steyn is a member of the Law Society’s panel of experts on evictions.

Sound Up Cilna Steyn
Macfarlane: Cilna, when I’m listening to everything that you’re telling me, it seems like the system is prejudiced against the owner?

Cilna: The thing is the fact that you need a court order to achieve something, doesn’t mean it’s unfair or unachievable. It means that we are in a country of more than 50 million people, we can’t be in a position of anarchy where everybody decides the law for themselves. We have a legal system that we have to follow if we want to live in a safe, just society.

Sound Up Shimi
Macfarlane: Why are you struggling to evict them, why is the process taking so long?

Shimi: It’s a legal process. And every time there is either lawyers or people appealing for the case to be rescinded. Sometimes they don’t pitch up in court and then later on the ask for rescission of the matter.

Voice
The South African Police Service has not granted our request for an interview and in a written response said they are still investigating the allegations. Peter Ngaula denied all the allegations against him in an email, and said “my family and I have been treated badly and threatened, so we are not safe”. Meanwhile owners like Mahlaela are stuck with footing the bills for bond repayments, utilities and levies on houses they do not have access to.

Sound Up Cilna Steyn Macfarlane: Cilna, when I’m listening to everything that you’re telling me, it seems like the system is prejudiced against the owner? Cilna: The thing is the fact that you need a court order to achieve something, doesn’t mean it’s unfair or unachievable. It means that we are in a country of more than 50 million people, we can’t be in a position of anarchy where everybody decides the law for themselves. We have a legal system that we have to follow if we want to live in a safe, just society. Sound Up Shimi Macfarlane: Why are you struggling to evict them, why is the process taking so long? Shimi: It’s a legal process. And every time there is either lawyers or people appealing for the case to be rescinded. Sometimes they don’t pitch up in court and then later on the ask for rescission of the matter. Voice The South African Police Service has not granted our request for an interview and in a written response said they are still investigating the allegations. Peter Ngaula denied all the allegations against him in an email, and said “my family and I have been treated badly and threatened, so we are not safe”. Meanwhile owners like Mahlaela are stuck with footing the bills for bond repayments, utilities and levies on houses they do not have access to.
